tasks.title: Introduce owned lossless shared GPU preview surfaces

Full G0 passed. Full corpus G3 passed. Corrected recovery witness passed 24 exact frames, device loss, producer and renderer crashes, cache, resize and no residual sessions. This development completion does not claim final M11 performance or exit acceptance.

tasks.title: Serve time-addressed native project preview snapshots
tasks.scope: Use immutable project snapshots and exact revision/composition/time/target identity with NativeProjectSession; retain only authenticated M5 rasters and native media grants across bounded requests.
tasks.progress: Committed immutable time-addressed project snapshots with trusted last-valid plugin packages, content-bound scope, registry invalidation and explicit unavailable-generator semantics for root and nested scenes. tasks.title: Integrate the Electron preview broker and renderer receiver
tasks.scope: Own the sidecar, imported textures, VideoFrames and release acknowledgements; reject stale generations and cleanly drain cancellation, resize, project replacement and renderer teardown.
tasks.progress: Audited committed broker, client, host and receiver ownership against unchanged execution identity and current full G0 / real-host recovery. No implementation changes or new pixel results. Full M11 exit remains pending.

tasks.title: Present native frames in the editor viewport
tasks.scope: Route beauty and supported diagnostic previews through native evaluation; preserve exact paused and direct-manipulation times, adapter identity and explicit capability fallback.
tasks.progress: Native viewport presentation now includes serialized exact-time comparison snapshots preserving diagnostic mode and selection, independently bounded canvases and stale-context rejection. Full G0 and real Electron snapshots/recovery pass. Full editor workflow qualification remains in T6; M11 exit is not claimed.

tasks.title: Integrate RAM preview caching and idle prerender
tasks.scope: Cache completed native frames with existing revision/time/target scopes; preserve budget, cancellation, displayed frame and asynchronous lifetime semantics.
tasks.progress: Native cache retains existing revision/target/AA/plugin scopes and exact paused times. Idle scheduling now uses bounded iteration instead of allocating the full work-area frame list. Tests prove byte-budget shrinkage, cache hits, wrap order, and stale idle rejection on revision, quality and playback changes. Real host cache, snapshots, resize and device/producer/renderer recovery passed. Full milestone exit remains pending.

tasks.title: Verify complete native preview pixels and application lifecycle
tasks.scope: Cover corpus and owner-project preview outputs, edits, resize, stale completion, cache and teardown through real Electron presentation; self-review all non-exact results.
tasks.progress: Actual editor interaction coverage passes 18 exact frames (cycle143). Installed-plugin root/nested lifecycle now passes 18 exact paired frames including live registry invalidation, valid/rejected reload, disable/enable, safe-mode recovery and removal. Debug bridge build/pin prevents stale development executable qualification. Full G0 passes. T6 coverage implementation and affected targeted checks are complete; prior complete corpus coverage remains recorded, and current-source corpus/owner preview refresh is deferred to the M11 full exit under the approved layered policy.

tasks.progress: Current same-invocation formal three-pair throughput and input-to-compositor latency acceptance passed with all required preview gates and the exit audit. Seven canonical scenarios, complete raw samples, owner inputs, execution source and actual binaries are authenticated.

tasks.title: Complete the Rust preview exit audit
tasks.scope: Bind all current G0/G3/G4/G6 evidence to production native preview, complete task coverage and synchronized docs before M12 retires the TS GPU renderer.
tasks.progress: Current complete G0/G3/G4/G6 invocation and production preview exit audit passed. All 337 cases / 1819 frames, editor and plugin workflows, lifecycle recovery and packaged binaries are authenticated. Historical failed runs remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Complete native export audio and control semantics
tasks.scope: Honor immutable includeAudio selection and acknowledge pauses at safe native processing boundaries; retain cancellation and atomic publication behavior.
tasks.progress: Output audio selection and correlated safe-boundary pause receipts are implemented. Real native exports validate unchanged reactive plans/RGB/NV12 when muted, repeated acknowledged pause/resume, cancellation, controller disconnect, malformed controls and atomic cleanup. Queue integration remains explicitly owned by M12-T4.

tasks.title: Render native PNG stills and sequences
tasks.scope: Reuse one native project session for bounded time-addressed PNG outputs, with control, progress and complete-output receipts.
tasks.progress: Native PNG still and sequence outputs reuse one project session, preserve RGBA and odd dimensions, bind rational frame times and hashes, and support acknowledged pause/cancel with atomic bounded publication. Real spectrum PNG frames exactly match video-path pre-encode RGBA; 321x181 text at 30000/1001, default still count, lifecycle cleanup and existing-output preservation pass. Production queue integration remains M12-T4.

tasks.title: Materialize immutable native queue projects
tasks.scope: Bind queue project snapshots to authorized immutable media, retained raster capabilities and trusted installed-plugin packages.
tasks.progress: Immutable project/media/plugin assembly is complete. Rust upgrades historical private queue copies; receipts bind authored and normalized hashes. Legacy locator identities and frozen bytes are authenticated separately, and native decoders receive verified byte digests. Composition dimensions, rational clock and frame range are checked. Fifteen exact real exports cover historical image/video/audio, advanced media, PSD fallback, 4100-frame sequence admission, inputs above 64 MiB, text and lighting. Two disabled-plugin checks and full G0 pass. Production queue routing, long-job streaming and delivery qualification remain in M12-T4 and later tasks.

tasks.title: Implement the native project queue worker
tasks.scope: Drive native project outputs from Electron main with correlated progress, pause/resume/cancel, cleanup and atomic multi-output publication.
tasks.progress: Native project queue worker implementation is complete: immutable inputs and plugins, correlated progress/control, retained media leases, atomic mixed-output publication, cancellation/cleanup, exact lazy frame schedules, incremental media admission, streamed receipts and bounded audio staging. Application main selects NativeQueueHostFactory with ASTER_NATIVE_QUEUE=1 and uses its application-owned runtime and plugin resolver. The actual background application completes PNG still, 12-frame sequence and 12-frame H.264/AAC jobs through native workers, persists all completion records, uses no hidden-host IPC and clears its temporary jobs. G0 passes. Default route retirement, remaining production capability/limit coverage and full milestone gates remain M12-T5 through M12-T9 work.

tasks.title: Select native preview and isolate the TS oracle
tasks.scope: Make production preview native by default, preserve Canvas2D compatibility behavior and isolate the retained TS GPU renderer to explicit reference tooling.
tasks.progress: Native preview selection and TS reference isolation are implemented. Production uses an independent presentation beauty contract and unchanged Canvas compatibility adapter; reference sessions explicitly import the immutable TS renderer and original beauty adapter. Ordinary Vite builds reject those modules and the old RenderHost in emitted chunks; separate reference builds must retain the TS constructor. Application startup no longer registers or launches hidden TS hosts, and queue exports default to native project workers. Eighteen editor diagnostic/move/drag witnesses remain exact, Canvas capture/resize passes, and the actual application completes still/sequence/H.264-AAC jobs without native enable flags or hidden-host IPC. Full G0 passes. Final packaged workflows, capability limits and complete milestone gates remain pending.

tasks.title: Retire every production TS render entry point
tasks.scope: Route foreground/background queue, automation, capture and supported output types through native project rendering; remove silent TS GPU fallbacks.
tasks.progress: Production preview, foreground/background queue, automation and capture route through native project rendering with no silent TS GPU fallback. Old browser export IPC is retired and normal bundles exclude all four retained reference entry modules. Streamed media, optional PNG disk budgets and aligned 2 GiB video limits are qualified. MP4 total deadlines are optional; explicit deadlines release paused producers on mux failure while preserving the failure cause and atomic cleanup. Current real native lifecycle, repeated controls, exact pause witnesses, three actual application outputs and full G0 pass. Packaged/foreground delivery qualification remains M12-T8 and complete current-source gate acceptance remains M12-T7/T9.
tasks.delivery_qualification: Implementation complete under layered-development-verification-v1; not a milestone exit. M12-T8 owns packaged/foreground workflows and synchronized delivery documentation; M12-T9 requires the full M12 verifier.

tasks.title: Compose final production migration gates
tasks.scope: Wire current native G1/G2/G3/G4/G5/G6 evidence and a complete retirement audit into the full M12 verifier.
tasks.progress: M12 G1/G2/G3/G4/G5 routing is implemented. G4 now serially composes balanced Rust-authored-project/retained-TS export pairs with existing complete preview throughput and latency. Original protocols, inputs, audio, active GPU, hardware, binaries and on-disk evidence are authenticated. G6 delivery/retirement and M12 exit remain unimplemented; complete gates remain pending.

native_build_entrypoints_increment.implementation: Shipping, IR, native core, encoded quality, standalone NV12, retained native observations, TS pixels and parity capture/oracle share scripts/native-build.mjs. This prevents later verification stages from replacing the jointly selected CLI with a standalone feature graph.

owner_current_paired_increment.scope: owner-main only, four full-length matched pairs against retained TS with excluded per-run warm-up; no CPU sampling and no full G4 acceptance from this subset
owner_current_paired_increment.reason: Measure end-to-end impact of the implemented descriptor-hash cache using the now pixel-verified shipping binary; isolated hashing improvement was not export performance evidence.

native_resource_delta_increment.implementation: Frame IPC references only resources in the immediately preceding successfully admitted frame. Main retains control metadata, logical payload size and admitted identity, not repeated payload bytes. Native resource window independently requires each reference to remain installed. Full logical byte/resource budgets, whole-job mutation checks and cancellation ordering remain enforced.

evidence_for_change.scope: Historical all-pixel replay inventory only. Superseded as native IPC evidence: file-image pixels are excluded from native plan-only transfer.

native_resource_delta_increment.failure_analysis: Initial hardware test incorrectly required binary savings where only zero-byte descriptors repeated; both decoded outputs were already identical. Corrected fresh test covers both groups with equal decoded hashes and logical budgets. First owner observation exposed missing optional-field allowance at the RenderHost IPC parser; fixed and routed preflight tests through the actual parser. No performance result from failed observation.
native_resource_delta_increment.performance_interpretation: One current 300-frame observation reached 14.0193 FPS / 21399 ms versus historical pre-change native paired median 12.1022 FPS and TS 30.1215 FPS. Directional improvement only; no repeated contemporaneous pair or performance acceptance. Current plan-wall median remains 53.3 ms. Stage timings overlap and are not additive.
native_resource_delta_increment.next_step: Reduce measured production plan preparation overhead while retaining immutable capture ownership and admission budgets; avoid another paired matrix until native can exceed retained TS.

native_packet_copy_increment.implementation: Production packet construction receives the preceding resource closure, so retained resource bytes are never copied into a disposable IPC packet. Speculative capture may use the pending frame closure, but is discarded unless admission succeeds. New payload snapshots and full logical budgets are preserved. Production and native benchmark use the same path.
native_packet_copy_increment.performance_interpretation: Single observation only: 14.5455 FPS / 20624.9 ms; preceding single resource-reference observation was 14.0193 FPS / 21399 ms. Plan-wall median 51.1 ms versus 53.3 ms. Small directional change does not prove repeated performance gain or full G4 acceptance.

native_snapshot_unicode_increment.implementation: Verified raster snapshots copy their pixel view into an independent compact Uint8Array and clone metadata separately, including the pre-await verification snapshot. Unicode scalar validation uses a Unicode-mode surrogate-range regex, preserving rejection of unpaired UTF-16 without per-character JavaScript iteration.
native_snapshot_unicode_increment.diagnostic_failure_reason: Copied opt-in Electron runner initially resolved preload relative to its diagnostic directory. Its exact test process was stopped; corrected absolute preload path ran in a fresh directory. No product defect or accepted performance from that failure.
native_snapshot_unicode_increment.profile_scope: 300 measured owner frames after warm-up; sampling is diagnostic only, not G4 evidence. Aggregated self samples: canonical JSON 2184.705 ms; SHA process 1857.001 ms; verified pixel copy 1768.900 ms; Unicode scan 808.072 ms.
native_snapshot_unicode_increment.performance_interpretation: One unsampled observation reached 14.7601 FPS / 20325.1 ms and median plan-wall 49.85 ms. Prior single observation was 14.5455 FPS / 20624.9 ms / 51.1 ms. This small difference does not prove a stable gain; native remains below historical retained TS median 30.1215 FPS.

native_media_identity_cache_increment.implementation: Media hashes may select private validated descriptor snapshots, but only complete structural equality and empty payloads permit reuse. Snapshots are parsed from the exact canonical text hashed. Both lookup maps share FIFO eviction, a 4096-entry bound and a 4 MiB text-plus-snapshot string budget; binary hashing is unchanged.
native_media_identity_cache_increment.regressions: Changed fields, forged hints, malformed Unicode, extra fields, unexpected bytes, independent ownership and eviction preserve rejection or recomputation.
native_media_identity_cache_increment.performance_interpretation: Single unsampled observation: 15.81036 FPS / 18974.9 ms; median plan-wall 44.7 ms. Previous single observation 14.76007 FPS / 20325.1 ms / 49.85 ms. Direction supports keeping the increment but is not a repeated contemporaneous paired gate. Native remains below retained TS historical median 30.12155 FPS.

native_identity_clone_increment.implementation: Compare the live media identity against private verified cached descriptors before cloning. Cache misses snapshot complete source/frame content before hashing; all returned messages remain independent clones. Nested source IDs and raster sample arrays cannot mutate the private cache.
native_identity_clone_increment.performance_interpretation: One unsampled observation reached 16.29797 FPS / 18407.2 ms and 42.5 ms median plan preparation. Prior single result was 15.81036 FPS / 18974.9 ms / 44.7 ms. No repeated paired acceptance; native remains below retained TS.

native_source_identity_probe.finding: MediaGrants.read always scans source bytes for FNV64 even when identity already equals the computed SHA-256 identity. Historical pinned owner video source has a sha256 identity. The current observation measures 4492.7629 ms in native input preparation, but the portion caused by this scan is not measured.
native_source_identity_probe.next_increment: Check the granted SHA-256 first, then compute legacy FNV only if needed to match the requested identity. Preserve fresh file reading, byte limits, cancellation, scope/member checks and changed-content rejection. No new dependency or snapshot cache is needed.

native_source_identity_increment.implementation: Fresh granted SHA-256 bytes bypass the unused legacy FNV scan. Legacy requests still compute FNV after SHA authorization. Fresh reads, bounds, cancellation and scope/member checks remain intact. No snapshot cache or dependency added.
native_source_identity_increment.performance_interpretation: Single owner observation 16.313657 FPS versus prior 16.297970 FPS is essentially unchanged; no material end-to-end gain established. Native input preparation 4461.1048 ms versus 4492.7629 ms. G4 remains unaccepted.

canonical_string_increment.implementation: Bounded cache of validated immutable long-string JSON escaping; 4096 entries and 4 MiB original plus escaped UTF-16 storage. All object/array traversal and invalid input rejection remain unchanged.
canonical_string_increment.scope: Historical serialization microbenchmark; no export acceptance.
canonical_string_increment.verdict: Local serialization is faster but owner export remains 16.285672 FPS versus 16.313657 FPS before the experiment. Extra cache and its tests/docs were removed. canonical.ts restored byte-for-byte to the pre-experiment source hash. No G4 acceptance.

current_cpu_attribution.finding: Most sampled SHA-256 work comes from PrecompositionBundleResources.addPlan -> contentResourceHashSync while assembling frame and effect plans (1065.927 ms and 600.024 ms in the two largest call stacks). The repeated canonical JSON cost is now mostly plan metadata encoding, not long media identity strings.
current_cpu_attribution.scope: CPU attribution from instrumented owner export only; FPS is not performance acceptance. No source mutation occurred during capture.

async_plan_hash_increment.implementation: Native-only assembly encodes producer inputs into private FPLN bytes synchronously, then hashes plans of at least 16 KiB through WebCrypto (at most 32 active hashes / 64 MiB encoded in-flight bytes). Small plans and pressure fallback use existing synchronous SHA. All digests and dependencies remain authenticated; independent raster owners survive assembly waits and release on success/failure/abort. No extra complete-input snapshot or equality cache remains.

first_attempt.verdict: Rejected: extra full input snapshots and byte comparison outweighed accelerated hashing; replaced by direct owned encoding.

async_plan_hash_increment.sequencing_fix: Collect and independently encode producer data before textures.flush consumes pending temporal raster passes. The GPU upload failure path aborts pending readback and drains the assembly while releasing its independent raster lease.

rejected_capture.verdict: Rejected exact-plan mismatch: temporal raster plans were collected after flush consumed them. Fixed collection ordering; capture v2 passes all six exact frames. This is a plan comparison failure, not an accepted pixel residual.

pre_fix_observation.verdict: Not used as correctness-qualified performance evidence because subsequent production capture exposed a temporal plan omission.

async_plan_hash_increment.performance_interpretation: Corrected single owner observation 16.665185 FPS / 18001.6 ms / 41.1 ms median preparation versus prior valid 16.313657 FPS / 18389.5 ms / 42.2 ms. Small observed improvement, not paired acceptance; native remains below retained TS.

direct_native_packet_increment.implementation: Native packet capture uses brand-authenticated VerifiedMediaPixels directly. Full logical budgets and declared raster identity/coverage are checked before serialization. New raster bytes are copied once at packet creation; retained references avoid intermediate payload copies. Private arrays never escape, and descriptors/returned packets remain independent. Packet and diagnostic capture retain cancellation/failure/GPU submission ownership semantics. Shipping RenderHost and the owner performance runtime use the same direct packet path.
direct_native_packet_increment.performance_interpretation: One owner observation improved from 16.665185 FPS to the recorded result; full paired native performance acceptance remains outstanding. Shipping RenderHost and the owner runtime exercise identical direct packet capture.

stage_attribution.interpretation: Across 300 frames, main-process resource installation was 1933.53 ms and native render/encode requests 9587.41 ms. Rust input preparation was 4398.35 ms, frame validation 1986.32 ms and output completion 2400.67 ms. These nested/overlapped intervals must not be added to derive export wall time; no finer source of input preparation has been measured.

video_window32_increment.implementation: Increase default video lookahead from 8 to 32 presentation frames within the unchanged 16 MiB byte budget and existing 64-frame configurable hard cap. Source authorization, timestamp selection, cancellation and bounded window replacement are unchanged. Retain eight-frame gate coverage and add explicit default-size coverage.
video_window32_increment.motivation: Current owner observation attributes 4398.35 ms to native input preparation. Pinned historical owner video is 320x80 (102400 bytes/frame); the eight-frame default caps reuse well below the existing byte budget. This is a bounded startup-amortization hypothesis, not a measured attribution to process startup.

pixel_review_reuse.reason: The pixel gate revalidated all 44 existing section 6.6 accepted decode reviews against identical reference/candidate RGBA hashes, metrics, structural checks and pinned report/contact-sheet/heatmap evidence. The independent audit additionally proves every current native output is exact against the historical native output. No new pixel residual or tolerance is introduced.

transport.reason: Shared transport initialization failed: Native sidecar closed (3221225477) before a clean shutdown during begin_export:
transport.interpretation: Shared begin_export again exited with 3221225477 before admitting any frame. Existing bounded fresh-process readback qualification completed all 300 native frames with hardware encoding. This does not fix or accept the historical driver failure.

video_window32_increment.performance_interpretation: Single 300-frame observation: 20.89631 FPS / 14356.6 ms, compared with prior single 18.54175 FPS / 16179.7 ms. Native input preparation decreased from 4398.35 ms to 2341.71 ms, supporting bounded decode startup amortization. Transport differs (prior shared; current readback following initialization failure), so this is not a matched performance comparison or G4 acceptance. Measured preparation before warm-up was 5367.74 ms versus 2867.86 ms and is preserved separately; the reporting convention is unchanged.

nested_validation_increment.implementation: Runtime dependency traversal relies on the decoder canonicality checks and skips redundant reconstruction of unchanged nested plans. The explicit ir bundle audit keeps nested byte-for-byte reconstruction through with_roundtrip. Resource-closure membership uses a per-traversal ordered set; no persistent cache or validation bypass is added.
nested_validation_increment.pixel_review_reuse: All six non-exact decode comparisons exactly match existing accepted reference/candidate RGBA hashes, metrics and structural checks; the gate revalidates their section 6.6 evidence. Independent audit confirms current native output is byte-exact against historical native output. No new residual or tolerance change.
nested_validation_increment.performance_interpretation: Runtime frame validation decreased from 2035.45 ms to 1408.85 ms across 300 frames. Overall single-observation throughput was 20.93043 FPS / 14333.2 ms versus 20.89631 FPS / 14356.6 ms, which does not demonstrate an end-to-end gain. Current transport is nv12-shared; preceding window32 observation used readback after shared initialization failure. Retain this small implementation simplification and demonstrated reduction of redundant work, without claiming paired acceptance or driver repair.

wire_copy_increment.implementation: Already validated media identity pairs and binding-lease resource messages copy plain object/array trees without serializing immutable strings. Original untrusted-input snapshot, validation, hashing, private cache ownership and binary payload copies are unchanged.
wire_copy_increment.profile_evidence: Updated 300-frame profile has 15034 ms sampled duration; exclusive mediaFrameMessages 782 ms and resourceMessages getter 553 ms. Both serialize already verified message trees, including large immutable strings. Sampling is diagnostic, not performance acceptance.
wire_copy_increment.performance_interpretation: One owner observation reached 22.89220 FPS / 13104.9 ms with plan-wall median 29.8 ms, compared with preceding 20.93043 FPS / 14333.2 ms / 33.9 ms. Both observations selected nv12-shared. This supports the implementation but is not a repeated contemporaneous paired G4 acceptance. Native remains below the historical retained TS 30.12155 FPS.
wire_copy_increment.validation_note: Initial targeted unit tests passed. Typecheck then caught an unsupported Object.hasOwn use in the new test (ES library target); the test now uses Object.getOwnPropertyNames. Final typecheck, Biome and full G0 passed with no product API requirement change.

store_copy_increment.implementation: Bundle-store and GPU registry metadata use the existing validated plain-wire copy. All descriptor validation, content hashing, GPU generation checks and binary buffer ownership remain intact, including pre-await asynchronous snapshots.
store_copy_increment.validation_note: Initial new tests supplied an invalid bare UTF-16 array and were correctly rejected. Fixtures were corrected to the existing utf16_units object representation; final targeted tests and all type checks pass.
store_copy_increment.performance_interpretation: Single shared-transport owner observation is 22.47932 FPS versus preceding 22.89220 FPS. Median preparation is 28.9 ms versus 29.8 ms, but admission increased from 10597.27 to 11087.53 ms. No end-to-end speedup or paired G4 acceptance is established. Retained as a small consistent use of the already tested copy helper; next work targets admission/producer overlap rather than additional speculative clone substitutions.

retained_metadata_increment.implementation: Already admitted resource references reuse private metadata snapshots. Consumer inputs receive independently copied plain-wire metadata and control buffers. New snapshots are captured before consumer access and published only after successful admission. The shared copy helper is now in dependency-free core code for both browser and NodeNext Electron builds. All input budgets, content authentication, sequencing and cancellation remain required.
retained_metadata_increment.diagnostic_conclusion: Admission was longer than overlapping preparation for 289/300 frames; only 51.7 ms of preparation exceeded admission. Encoded spool writes cost 85.27 ms, while ownInput cost 985.68 ms and retainMetadata 604.89 ms. This rejected deeper lookahead and disk buffering as the next change.
retained_metadata_increment.validation_note: Two preserved candidate builds failed when directly importing renderer canonical code under Electron NodeNext. The utility was extracted to a dependency-free shared core module; final type checks, build, complete tests and real exports pass.

production_job_transports.reason: Shared transport initialization failed: Native sidecar closed (3221225477) before a clean shutdown during begin_export:

retained_metadata_increment.performance_interpretation: Single shared-transport owner export reached 23.80027 FPS, compared with 23.18643 FPS in the instrumented pre-change observation. ownInput fell from 985.68 to 661.40 ms and retainMetadata from 604.89 to 72.26 ms; admission fell from 10674.63 to 9803.62 ms. This is not repeated paired G4 acceptance and remains below historical retained TS throughput.

video_window128_increment.implementation: Default and maximum configurable decode-window frame count are 128. The existing 16 MiB default byte budget, single-window replacement, timestamp selection, authorization, timeout and cancellation remain unchanged. Window validation preserves explicit eight- and 32-frame modes and adds the new default mode.
video_window128_increment.motivation: Previously pinned owner video is 320x80, or 102400 bytes per RGBA frame. A 128-frame window uses 13107200 bytes, within the existing 16777216-byte budget, amortizing repeated process startup without enlarging the byte budget.

pixel_review_reuse.reason: Current native outputs match historical native RGBA exactly. All 44 non-exact TS decode comparisons revalidated existing section 6.6 self-review records against identical image hashes, metrics, structural checks, contact sheets and heatmaps. No new residual or tolerance is introduced.

video_window128_increment.performance_interpretation: Single shared-transport owner export reached 24.97066 FPS / 12014.1 ms versus preceding 23.80027 FPS / 12604.9 ms. Native input preparation fell from 2314.51 to 1642.65 ms. Preparation increased from 2847.31 to 3014.28 ms and ten-frame warmup from 1448.77 to 1935.56 ms; both remain explicitly reported using the unchanged timing convention. This is not repeated paired G4 acceptance and remains below historical retained TS throughput.

resource_frame_coalescing_experiment.implementation: Experiment coalesced the final batch of at most 64 resource commands with render_frame, preserving ordered acknowledgement validation, aggregate payload bounds, caller-owned bytes and one active transaction. It passed controls but did not establish end-to-end speedup, so all implementation, tests and documentation were restored.
resource_frame_coalescing_experiment.performance_interpretation: Single shared-transport candidate measured 24.64005 FPS versus preceding 24.97066 FPS. No gain justifies extra protocol complexity. This is not paired G4 acceptance.

full_g0_reuse.reason: All executable/fixture/doc sources except the ledger match the preceding verified source fingerprint exactly after reversion. The Electron output was rebuilt from restored sources; no new implementation remains.

resource_frame_coalescing_experiment.hardware_note: Recursive control again used existing readback qualification after shared initialization exited with 3221225477; the fault is not repaired or reclassified.

native_unicode_increment.implementation: Unicode scalar validation uses native String.isWellFormed where available with the unchanged Unicode-regex fallback. Serialization, canonical keys, safe integer rules, output bytes and rejection codes are unchanged.
native_unicode_increment.performance_interpretation: One shared-transport owner export reached 25.21199 FPS versus preceding 24.97066 FPS. Median plan preparation fell from 29.0 to 27.6 ms. The small single-observation difference is not repeated paired G4 acceptance and remains below historical retained TS median 30.12155 FPS.

decoded_plans_increment.implementation: Complete dependency validation can deliver individually validated owned plans to a visitor. SuppliedFrame retains immutable Arc-owned plans for one assembly, sharing them across root, layer, generator, surface and temporal stages. Retained encoded bytes are bounded by the caller container limit; excess uses full decoding with the original limits. All canonical, typed-blob, closure, contract and header checks remain mandatory; failed closure discards the private table.
decoded_plans_increment.performance_interpretation: One shared-transport owner export reached 26.11648 FPS versus preceding 25.21199 FPS. Native frame validation fell from 1501.59 to 1102.68 ms over 300 frames. This remains a single observation below historical retained TS median 30.12155 FPS, not repeated paired G4 acceptance.

canonical_tree_increment.implementation: Canonical JSON validates and orders an independent tree before native serialization. Numeric-looking keys and sparse arrays use the token serializer on the prepared tree, preserving lexical key order and existing bytes without rereading input getters. Primitive fast path, safe integers, plain-object rules, ASCII keys, Unicode checks and special own prototype keys retain existing semantics.
canonical_tree_increment.performance_interpretation: Ordered-tree serialization roughly halves the offline metadata sample cost. One shared-transport owner export reached 26.50341 FPS versus preceding 26.11648 FPS, with median preparation 25.8 ms versus 27.05 ms. This small single-observation gain is not paired G4 acceptance and remains below historical retained TS median 30.12155 FPS.

video_prefetch_increment.implementation: One adjacent video window can decode asynchronously while the current window is consumed. Both share the existing 16 MiB / 128-frame allowance; pending allocation is reserved explicitly. Every window retains full process exit/error/extent validation. Drop, cancellation, source switch and authorization failure cancel and join work. Prefetch only pins a snapshot already accounted in the source cache; source switching joins old work before cache eviction. Disabled, small and uncached-source modes remain synchronous; explicit prefetch-off is available for comparison.

video_prefetch_increment.validation_repair: Initial gate sequence crossed source identity before the intended prefetch hit; adjusted it to exercise an adjacent same-source range. The first failure remains retained. After the initial pass, added source-snapshot accounting guards and explicit uncached-source controls; the final v3 suite passes.
video_prefetch_increment.performance_interpretation: One owner export reached 30.22335 FPS / 9926.1 ms, versus preceding 26.50341 FPS / 11319.3 ms. Native input preparation fell from 1626.10 to 161.56 ms. Transport changed to qualified NV12 readback after shared initialization AV (3221225477); initialization 5222.67 ms and ten-frame warmup 1604.73 ms remain explicitly recorded outside the unchanged measurement interval. Neither a matched transport gain nor paired G4 acceptance is claimed.

opening_cache_increment.implementation: Export reports retain the latest cumulative media/video/texture cache statistics, including warm-up; the response boxes the timing snapshot to keep the enum bounded. Decoded media default retention is 128 MiB with unchanged 256-entry cap; explicit limits and zero-disabled semantics remain. Pixel conversion, authorization and individual decode/registry budgets are unchanged.

candidate_transport.transportReason: Shared transport initialization failed: Native sidecar closed (3221225477) before a clean shutdown during begin_export:

opening_cache_increment.interpretation: The first complete five-workload pair found native opening 4.9178 FPS versus TS 16.243 FPS despite four other native workloads being faster. Stopped pair 2 intentionally; its missing report error was induced by termination and is not a product failure. Counters then showed 548 media decodes/518 evictions and only 36 video decoder calls. Raising bounded retention to 128 MiB lowered decodes to 190/145 evictions, input preparation to 29067.49 ms, and improved single opening FPS from 4.82582 to 8.21129. Both diagnostic and candidate used shared NV12 with stable sources. This is not a repeated paired or pixel-quality acceptance.

quota_pause.reason: User explicitly requested stopping when remaining Codex quota reaches 5%. All current full G0 checks pass; M8 remains incomplete.
quota_pause.resume_step: Continue M8-T1 from the demonstrated owner-opening bottleneck. The 128 MiB decoded-media cache reduces decodes 548 to 190 and input preparation 90.44 s to 29.07 s, but opening 8.2113 FPS remains below contemporaneous first-pair TS 16.243 FPS; output completion remains 38.54 s. Investigate the bounded active image working set and GPU/output cost before another full paired matrix. Current full G3/G5/G6 and four-pair G4 acceptance remain required. Do not repeat already passing checks without a new change.

frame_cache_increment.implementation: Batch decode protects requested file-media hashes from eviction by other misses in the same frame. Oversized working sets decode uncached entries without displacing current-frame hits; other old entries retain LRU eviction. Protection is lexical to a call and cannot survive errors or cancellation. The 128 MiB / 256-entry limits are unchanged.
frame_cache_increment.performance_interpretation: One current shared-NV12 opening export reaches 11.11409 FPS, compared with preceding 8.21129. Input preparation decreases 29067.49 to 12944.30 ms, media decodes 190 to 106, and evictions 145 to 31 under the same retention budget. Output completion also changes 38538.80 to 33088.60 ms across different days, so do not attribute the whole FPS improvement to cache policy or claim paired acceptance.

gpu_output_diagnostic.implementation: Keep output completion split into NV12 conversion/sharing/readback including prior GPU work, and encoder submission/backpressure. Report latest GPU image/layer cache session counters and accumulated measured effect-region counters. Pixel generation and cache policy remain unchanged after exact candidate restoration.
gpu_output_diagnostic.decision: Reject the layer-cache reuse-priority candidate: opening 10.43036 FPS did not improve on the immediately preceding 11.16459 FPS. Allocations declined 1907 to 1688 and hits rose 532 to 751, but NV12/GPU completion rose 32.23 to 35.19 s. All 5324 pixel comparisons were exact and the focused GPU pressure test passed; correctness alone is not performance acceptance. Do not reinterpret the old failure or rerun the same experiment.

effect_pipeline_specialization.implementation: Compile bounded variants of the shared post shader by reachable optical/color opcodes, after existing precision lowering. Prune unreachable cases and compact dead expressions. Admission is limited to opcodes 12,17,18,27,50,102,104,105,183; other programs use the unchanged generic pipeline. Default at most 16 variants per device; CLI zero disables. Parameter values never enter the key.
effect_pipeline_specialization.decision: Retain the bounded optical/color specialization: exact native output across 5324 comparisons, full G0 passed, and opening single-observation throughput rose from 11.16459 to 12.17012 FPS. GPU/NV12 completion fell from 32.23 to 21.05 s while render submission rose from 4.56 to 6.98 s. This is not paired G4 acceptance; native is still below the retained 16.243 FPS TS opening observation.

png_decode_review_repair.reason: The six earlier frame-cache review records omitted registration/sequence and used nested evidence values. The strict reviewer correctly rejected the incomplete latest record. Preserve that failure and append complete current comparison records; never weaken reviewStatus.

native_png_decode.implementation: Reuse the existing Windows WIC memory decoder for authorized non-interlaced 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG snapshots. Preserve source grants/SHA checks, extent and byte limits, canvas alpha rounding and cancellation/deadline rejection before publication. Other layouts/platforms use unchanged FFmpeg decoding. Shared WIC module also preserves existing JPEG texture behavior. Native still/sequence receipts and audits identify the actual PNG backend. No dependency or cache-budget increase.

layer_texture_recycling.implementation: After existing GPU completion, reassign evicted same-extent layer cache textures to new keys. Clear valid/pending state; retain admission order, byte reservation and content eviction counts. No spare pool or new dependency. Expose physical allocation reuses independently from content hits.

gpu_timestamp_diagnostics.implementation: Opt-in GPU timestamps on render-plan and serve, with fixed five-query capacity and 128 bytes of query buffers reserved from the GPU budget. Default execution requests no timestamp features and allocates no query buffers. Render and NV12 stages produce separate diagnostic intervals, with shared-NV12 coverage and map cleanup on failure.
gpu_timestamp_diagnostics.initial_failure_repaired: Updated the direct converter test caller for the new optional profiler argument.
gpu_timestamp_diagnostics.coverage_correction: Prior 5324 layer-cache comparisons cover 1315 feature frames and 16 surface frames in four configurations; they do not include owner-opening. This run separately pins and verifies the four frozen owner-opening frames from the historical NV12 corpus, each repeated four times.
gpu_timestamp_diagnostics.performance_caveat: Timestamp readback synchronizes execution. Whole-process plain/profiled durations differ in cache state and instrumentation and must not be used as a G4 throughput comparison.

uniform_effect_buffers_experiment.reason: Moving the verified effect subset from storage to bounded uniform arrays preserves pixels but does not reduce representative root-scene GPU execution. Revert the additional layout, capacity-key and upload complexity without repeating full G0, corpus or export throughput runs for the rejected candidate.
uniform_effect_buffers_experiment.initial_failure_repaired: Matched the device uniform-buffer limit u64 type before the passing build.

root_pass_gpu_diagnostics.behavior: Opt-in only; command/effect indices identify root passes, omitted passes are counted, and export totals do not retain per-frame pass lists. Default production allocates no diagnostic resources.
root_pass_gpu_diagnostics.finding: The 27-operation optical/color layer is dominant: representative frames 356/713 spend 16.35513/16.49933 ms there.
root_pass_gpu_diagnostics.repairs: Replace Copy with owned Clone for diagnostic timing records and update the SSAA test call with an absent profiler.

identity_power_experiment.reason: The exact exponent-one path preserved the representative pixels but full-export GPU/NV12 completion remained 21.08 s versus baseline 21.04 s. Its 15.53 FPS correlated with faster CPU stages and does not establish a shader benefit. Removed before the retained blur-sample-cache experiment.
identity_power_experiment.initial_failure_repaired: Naga Math source spans identify the pow token, not its complete argument list.

blur_sample_reuse.implementation: One private blur sample per fragment invocation keyed by exact UV and radius. Misses call the original shared sampler, preserving nine-tap ordering and LOD arithmetic. Scope is the existing verified opcode subset; generic programs and other invocation/frame state are unchanged.
blur_sample_reuse.g0_repairs: Pass None for the profiler in the existing SSAA test; supply the configured npm_execpath so lefthook child checks find pnpm. The pixel run finished before editing the test. This final test-only adjustment does not alter the measured renderer binary.

blur_paired_performance.scope: Four complete matched TS/Rust pairs on all five required workloads, ten excluded warm-up frames per observation, GPU timestamps disabled. No acceptance until the source-pinned final report passes.

blur_multi_entry_experiment.implementation: Two private recent blur samples per fragment invocation, keyed by exact UV and radius with move-to-front hits. Misses preserve the original shared nine-tap sampler and LOD arithmetic. Existing bounded opcode specialization and generic fallback remain intact.

blur_first_two_experiment.reason: Representative heavy layers are 11.8052/12.27372 ms; lower projected tap count did not reduce measured GPU time. Retained the prior two-entry LRU.

integrated_wipe_roughen_verification.scope: Current-source complete M8 gate run; no reference-domain or tolerance changes. G5 may remain failed under the unresolved RGB-domain rule. Independent G3 and complete G4 must be measured rather than inferred from focused evidence.

complete_rgb_corpus_increment.implementation: Complete M8 pre-encode RGB coverage by authenticating PNGs already produced by the NV12 corpus runner, comparing remaining frames to independent immutable TS references, and auditing their union with core RGB coverage at exit. No added render work, reference changes or tolerance changes.

complete_rgb_integrated_verification.source_scope: Evidence applies to pre-increment source. The run was stopped before any source or ledger modification. No new full acceptance is claimed.
complete_rgb_integrated_verification.next_step: Validate exact admission index byte accounting and per-schedule reference audit reuse. Run current G0/quick verification and one owner-main performance observation. Encoding reference-domain policy remains unapplied pending owner answer.

reference_audit_reuse_increment.scope: Reuse PixelInputs only within one serial export schedule. Preserve per-case input hash stability and full final source checks; do not cache across runs or weaken repair evidence.

known_boundaries.detail: The original example places its opaque Background above Animated Disc in the top-first layer model. All five TS reference frames are uniformly RGBA [48,63,97,255]. Preserve this existing output; the case does not establish visible animation or sequence identity. Generated moving scenes and real media sequences provide independent coverage.
The current TS sidecar rejects EXR. Real linear EXR bytes are retained for native decoder coverage; M0 does not claim a TS EXR reference.
The current TS effect compiler maps path masks to ellipse parameters. The path case claims schema coverage only; ellipse and rectangle have independent real mask cases.
Point-light shadows are not implemented by the TS path; directional and spot fixtures provide actual shadow coverage.
Capture must reject renderer diagnostics, media registry failures, unloaded plugin requests and audio-analysis decode warnings rather than accepting successful readback as resource correctness.

Precomposition textureCount is the existing full-resolution target budget (two per plain surface, five with effects), not the total GPUTexture allocation count. Effect pyramids and identity LUTs are outside that count; pyramid storage is included in estimated bytes. The repaired count guard and cache preserve the existing 20-target, pixel, byte and depth limits.

Stable particle instance order prevents atomic-append nondeterminism. Hidden slots now retain a bounded storage write and vertex visibility checks. The two 36-frame capture runs establish current-fixture repeatability, not performance equivalence or cross-driver determinism. M0 does not require G4; retain this cost for particle workload measurement in M7/G4.
